'''Roger Ellis Millsap''' (November 18, 1954 – May 9, 2014) was an American psychometrician known for his research on [[measurement invariance]].<ref name=ap>{{Cite journal |last=Markus |first=Keith A. |date=2015 |title=Roger Ellis Millsap (1954–2014). |journal=American Psychologist |language=en |volume=70 |issue=9 |pages=931 |doi=10.1037/a0039885 |pmid=26653321 |issn=1935-990X}}</ref><ref name=psychometrika>{{Cite journal |last=Maydeu-Olivares |first=Alberto |date=July 2014 |title=In Memoriam, Roger E. Millsap 1954–2014 |journal=Psychometrika |language=en |volume=79 |issue=3 |pages=355–356 |doi=10.1007/s11336-014-9421-1 |pmid=25077438 |issn=0033-3123|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Millsap was born on November 18, 1954, in [[Olympia, Washington|Olympia]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]]. He was the only child of Max Ellis Millsap, who was a general manager for the [[Olympia Oil and Wood]] company, and Lillian Rogers Millsap (née Turner), an executive director of two chapters of the [[Red Cross]].<ref name=ap/> He received his BS degree from the [[University of Washington]] in 1977, followed by an MA in [[statistics]] and a PhD in [[quantitative psychology]]. He received both of his advanced degrees in 1983 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he was supervised by Bill Meredith.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://psychology.clas.asu.edu/people/remembrance |title=In Remembrance  |website=Arizona State University |language=en |access-date=2018-09-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Millsap |first=Roger Ellis |title=A Probabilistic Model for Semantic Memory Retrieval |date=1983 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=University of California, Berkeley |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=R6RJAQAAMAAJ}}</ref>

After receiving his PhD, Millsap taught [[industrial/organizational psychology]] at [[Baruch College]] until 1997, where he eventually became a full professor. In 1997, he joined the quantitive psychology faculty of [[Arizona State University]], where he taught until his death in 2014. He served as [[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[Multivariate Behavioral Research]]'' from 1996 to 2006, and of ''[[Psychometrika]]'' from 2007 until his death. He also served as president of the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]] in 2001–2002, of Division 5 of the [[American Psychological Association]] in 2004–2005, and of the [[Psychometric Society]] in 2006–2007.<ref name=ap/><ref name=psychometrika/> His awards included the Society for Multivariate Experimental Psychology's [[Raymond Cattell]] Award (1993) and [[Herb Eber]] Award (2001), as well as three [[Jeffrey S. Tanaka#Legacy|Tanaka Awards]] (1995, 1999, and 2005) for work in ''[[Multivariate Behavioral Research]]''.<ref name=psychometrika/>

Millsap died suddenly on May 9, 2014. He was survived by his wife and four children.<ref name=psychometrika/>
